title: Session warmup orchestration — garden sketch
content:
Goal: brain-dump a lightweight, client-driven but server-coordinated pattern for warming LLM sessions to reduce first-response latency without blowing unit cost. This is intentionally messy — personal notebook to capture trade-offs, API shapes, and a toy orchestration model (the "garden" metaphor).

Context and motivation:
- Observed: cold-start tokens and KV cache fill cause 200–800ms extra latency tail for some conversational flows. In multi-tenant shared GPUs predictable warmup is tricky.
- Constraints: limited budget for pre-execution (can't run full model for every new session), need to respect per-tenant cost quotas, and avoid noisy signals that amplify warmups (spirals).
- Product goal: push 90th percentile interactive latency down by ~20–40ms for typical chat UIs while keeping warmup cost < 1.5x average per-session incremental cost.

Core idea (garden metaphor):
- Beds: logical warmup categories (e.g., "small prompt prefill", "function-call priming", "persona & tools"). Each bed has a policy and expected cost profile.
- Seeds: concrete warmup payloads (small prompt snippets, embedding prefetch, tool signatures). Seeds are cheap and targeted.
- Watering schedule: when to trigger seeds — on session creation, on specific client events, or probabilistic sampling.
- Garden keeper: a lightweight orchestration component (could be client-side + server hints) deciding which beds to water for a session.

Properties we want:
- Idempotent: warmup events can be replayed safely or deduped without corrupting KV cache state.
- Bounded cost: per-session budget + global budget enforcement.
- Signal-aware: warmup intensity adapts to signals (expected user intent, historical activity, client memory).
- Safe fallbacks: if a warmup fails or requests are throttled, fall back to on-demand inference.

API sketches (client & server):
1) Client registers session intent hint (tiny, optional):
POST /v1/sessions
{
  "client_session_id": "cid-1234",
  "intent_hint": ["compose_email", "summarize_page"],
  "warmup_pref": {"budget_ms": 100, "max_tokens_cost": 40}
}
- server response: includes warmup plan id and per-session budget token allowance.

2) Server warmup plan (sent as hint / pre-approved seeds the client can execute):
GET /v1/sessions/cid-1234/warmup-plan
Response body (example):
{
  "plan_id": "garden-202503-1",
  "beds": [
    {"id": "small-prefill", "seed": "intro: you are a helpful assistant...", "cost_est": 6},
    {"id": "tool-signature", "seed": "tool-list: calendar,search", "cost_est": 2}
  ],
  "budget_tokens": 32,
  "ttl_s": 900
}
Notes: the plan itself is advisory. The client may choose to execute seeds locally (if on-device) or ask the server to run them on the customer's warm pool.

3) Warmup execution call (idempotent):
POST /v1/warmups/exec
{
  "plan_id": "garden-202503-1",
  "session_id": "cid-1234",
  "bed_ids": ["small-prefill"],
  "mode": "background"  // background | foreground
}
Response: { "exec_id": "w-789", "accepted": true, "cost_charge": 5 }

- Exec call returns quickly; actual warm run can be scheduled on warm pool. If client is on same private deployment, execution could be local (fast).

Orchestration knobs (server-side):
- Global admission controller: enforces per-customer active warmup budget (tokens/ms), rejects new warmups when saturated.
- Priority scoring: sessions get warmup priority by ticket (paid tiers, sticky sessions, predicted intent probability).
- Sampled prober: occasionally run heavier warmups for cold users to collect telemetry and refresh sea of templates.

Heuristics and signals to decide bed watering:
- Session creation + explicit user intent -> strong candidate for small-prefill bed.
- Returning active sessions (within short TTL) -> minimal or no warmup.
- High-entropy instructions (code edit, complex planning) -> prefer larger prefill seeds (higher cost).
- UI-visible start (user starts typing) -> conservative background warmup until explicit send.

Cost accounting model (simple):
- Each seed has cost_est in tokens. Execution charges tokens from session budget and tenant budget.
- Warmup credits accrue on a rolling window; credits can be purchased (dedicated) or limited by free-tier.

Data & telemetry to collect (minimal):
- warmup.exec_id, plan_id, bed_id, start_ts, finish_ts, outcome (ok | throttled | failed), tokens_consumed, initial_user_latency_ms (first response), sample payload hashes (privacy-safe).
- Key analysis: correlate warmup presence with first-response latency reduction and per-session token delta.

Edge cases and failure modes:
- Spiral: client retries warmup on transient throttle => introduce client-side exponential backoff and server-side dedupe by plan_id+session_id.
- Privacy: seeds must not contain PII. Sanitize & strip sensitive user content from seeds and plan descriptors.
- Overfitting: if warmups use canonical prompts that differ from real user prompts, KV cache divergence could be useless — prefer seeds that match high-frequency real prefixes.

Prototyping experiments (short list):
- A/B: 50/50 sampling on web UI for small-prefill bed executed server-side vs no warmup. Measure 50th/95th latency and token delta.
- Budget enforcement: run synthetic load to validate admission controller prevents budget exhaustion.
- Signal tuning: use intent probability thresholds to vary bed selection and measure utility curves.

Sketch: state machine for client warmup orchestration (ASCII):

[client creates session] -> (send intent hint) -> [server returns plan/allowance]
   |
   v
[client chooses: local-exec?] -yes-> (execute seeds locally if on-device) -> [mark exec_done]
   |no
   v
[POST /warmups/exec] -> [server admission check] -> accepted? -> yes -> enqueue on warm pool -> exec -> report outcome
                                                |-> no -> return throttle + retry-after

Open questions / TODOs for next pass:
- How to encode seeds so they are compact, privacy-preserving, and expressive? (proto vs base64 vs compressed payload).
- Should warmup plans be pushable via streaming websocket to reduce RTT for plan fetch? (tradeoff: complexity).
- How to integrate with per-route rollouts & model variants (e.g., warmup seeds for quantized model variant vs full precision)? Plan needs model-compat metadata.
- Can we reuse prefix caching APIs (prefix-id) so that warmups can be referenced rather than re-sent? (I like this — introduce prefix registry).

Short checklist for an exploratory PR: 
- [ ] Minimal plan API + exec endpoint + telemetry events (backend + test harness)
- [ ] Client-side sample integration (web SDK) to send intent hint and optionally call exec
- [ ] Admission controller stub with simple token bucket per-tenant
- [ ] One A/B test setup (ui flag & server-side toggle)

Notes to self:
- Keep warmup seeds intentionally short (<= 64 tokens) for cheap experiments.
- Add a "skip-warmup" opt-out in SDK for power users wanting deterministic cold behavior.
- Remember: first-pass should be opt-in to avoid accidental cost blasts.

End of notebook. This is a very rough personal sketch — iterate later into a more formal spec (plan proto, exact fields, schemas, and RBAC considerations).
